entries.title: Target runtime compatibility
entries.summary: The bootstrap runtime is not the target runtime. Derive syntax/API/toolchain constraints from project evidence and preserve legacy compatibility unless migration is explicit.

entries.title: Separate product contract from technical design
entries.summary: Product specs define observable behavior; architecture/change documents define implementation boundaries and design decisions.

entries.title: Brownfield boundary preservation
entries.summary: Existing core modifications, overrides and conventions are evidence. Classify them before normalizing or replacing them.

entries.title: Secret handling
entries.summary: Secret values must not be copied into generated AI context, specs, memory, logs, baseline artifacts or prompts.

entries.title: Dependency manifests are evidence
entries.summary: Use declared dependency constraints and manifests to understand compatibility. A manifest graph is not a complete runtime call graph.

entries.title: Baseline comparison
entries.summary: A reference tree can identify added, missing and modified files, but the reference must match the target product/version before it is treated as authoritative.

entries.title: Extension lifecycle safety
entries.summary: Modules/plugins/extensions should preserve host compatibility, install/upgrade/uninstall lifecycle, permissions, data changes, translations and packaging.

entries.title: Migration safety
entries.summary: Schema/runtime migrations require impact analysis, forward/backward compatibility where relevant, rollback strategy and staged verification.
